# M15 source inputs

## bzip2 reconstruction

The controlled reconstruction target is bzip2 1.0.8, released 13 July 2019 by
Julian Seward. The upstream project provides the
[release archive](https://sourceware.org/pub/bzip2/bzip2-1.0.8.tar.gz),
[release information](https://sourceware.org/bzip2/downloads.html),
[checksum list](https://sourceware.org/pub/bzip2/sha512.sum) and
[manual and license terms](https://sourceware.org/bzip2/manual/manual.html).

`ports/bootstrap/inputs.json` pins these archive digests:

```text
SHA-256 ab5a03176ee106d3f0fa90e381da478ddae405918153cca248e682cd0c4a2269
SHA-512 083f5e675d73f3233c7930ebe20425a533feedeaaa9d8cc86831312a6581cefbe6ed0d08d2fa89be81082f2a5abdabca8b3c080bf97218a1bd59dc118a30b9f3
```

The SHA-512 matches the upstream published list. Both digests must match before
source preparation reads archive members. No upstream C/header patches are
applied. A selected set of unmodified files is copied to the generated source
workspace; per-file digests are recorded in `INPUTS.json` and `SOURCE.sha256`.
The selected files include all eight compiled C units, two headers, the original
Makefile, LICENSE, README, CHANGES, HTML manual and three compressed/reference
sample pairs. The optional PostScript manual and unrelated utility sources are
not required by this build recipe and are excluded from the bounded work disk.

The upstream bzip2 license remains unchanged in
`build/bootstrap/source/LICENSE` and `/persist/bootstrap/LICENSE`. Its copyright
and conditions continue to apply to bzip2/libbzip2 sources, documentation and
the reconstructed binary; these files are not relicensed as Apache-2.0.
Redistributed source must retain the upstream notice, conditions and disclaimer;
origin must remain accurate, altered upstream versions must be identified and
the author's name must not imply endorsement. Refer to the retained complete
license text for its exact terms.

The custom `ports/bootstrap/Makefile.anova`, preparation script, metadata and
first-party diagnostic/rejection fixtures are Apache-2.0. The custom recipe is
an additional build file, not a modified upstream Makefile. It directly links
the unmodified bzip2 compilation units with the prepared static musl/GCC
runtime. Any linked musl or GCC runtime code retains its own license and
applicable runtime exception. The seed compiler, binutils, make, sysroot and
their source-distribution boundaries remain documented in
[M11 compiler inputs](m11.md).

Host preparation supplies checksum-checked sources and the existing seed tools;
only guest GCC creates the bzip2 acceptance executable. The separately
host-compiled capacity diagnostic is first-party validation code and does not
count as source reconstruction or compiler bootstrap. Generated archives,
extracted sources, executable files and work disks remain under `build/` and
are not committed as first-party repository sources. Preserve the corresponding
upstream source, notices, input manifests and local recipe with any later
distribution. See [M15 profile](../M15_BOOTSTRAP.md) for the exact execution and
measurement boundaries.


## GCC feasibility inputs

The separate [M15.3 assessment](../M15_GCC.md) reuses the seven official source
archives locked in `ports/gcc/inputs.json`: GCC 11.2.0, binutils 2.37, make
4.4.1, musl 1.2.4, GMP 6.2.1, MPFR 4.1.0 and MPC 1.2.1. It verifies each
SHA-256 before auditing archive metadata. It neither extracts the full source
trees nor reconstructs any compiler component. The binary `bootstrap.tgz`
input is excluded from that source-tree count; inherited M11 binaries and
all corresponding-source requirements remain governed by [M11 inputs](m11.md).

`ports/bootstrap/gcc_probe.py` publishes only selected unchanged upstream
files under `build/bootstrap-gcc/source/`; the assessment imports them into
`/persist/gcc-probe`. Generated manifests record each original archive/member
and per-file hash. GCC's `configure`, `move-if-change`, `config.guess`,
`config.sub` and `install-sh` retain their individual copyright, copying
permissions and applicable exceptions. In particular, the generated configure
script grants unlimited copying/distribution/modification permission; do not
replace its notice with a blanket GPL or Apache declaration. The unmodified
GCC `COPYING3` is retained as `gcc-COPYING3`.

GCC's release-specific `INSTALL/prerequisites.html` is retained as
`gcc-prerequisites.html`. It is GNU Free Documentation License 1.3-or-later
material, with its original copyright and stated front/back-cover text
conditions preserved. The accompanying full `INSTALL/gfdl.html` is retained
as `gcc-gfdl.html`. No documentation text is relicensed as project code.

GMP `COPYING.LESSERv3` and `COPYINGv3`, MPFR `COPYING.LESSER` and `COPYING`,
and MPC `COPYING.LESSER` are retained under names prefixed with the upstream
component. They document the dependencies being assessed; copying these
notices does not install their headers, development libraries or sources into
the guest build environment. The existing GCC binary's linked dependencies
retain their [M11 license boundaries](m11.md).

The new audit, host orchestration, diagnostics and C++11 seed-test fixture are
first-party Apache-2.0 files. The host-built diagnostics provide no reconstructed
GCC component. The seed-test executable is built in guest from the first-party
fixture and linked against inherited M11 runtime libraries, whose original
terms and exceptions still apply. Generated upstream files, work disks and
executables remain below `build/` and are not copied into tracked first-party
sources. Preserve source identities, applicable notices and corresponding
source/recipe obligations in any later redistribution.
